introduction: Vermont Seasonal Fuel Assistance pays part of eligible households’ heating costs. It is separate from emergency Crisis Fuel.
description: Vermont Seasonal Fuel Assistance pays part of eligible households’ heating costs. It is separate from emergency Crisis Fuel.

sections.who: The state currently lists gross income at or below 185% of federal poverty. Homeowners and renters can qualify, including households paying heat through rent.
sections.get: Payment depends on the primary fuel and how heating costs are paid. Active recipients also qualify for free weatherization.
sections.docs:
• Household members, including people DCF may exclude from its fuel calculation.
  • Income evidence.
  • Heating fuel, supplier or rent information.
sections.apply:
1. Start or renew

    Previous recipients complete the annual review form. New applicants use the online link on Fuel Assistance.

  2. Choose paper if needed

    Call 800-479-6151 or use a district office; a fuel-only form is available.

  3. Return records

    Sign the form and supply the requested heating and income details.
sections.after: The benefit covers part of heating costs. For an immediate emergency, contact Crisis Fuel intake separately.
sections.sources: Content checked October 1, 2026 using Current DCF Fuel Assistance. Current eligibility and the final decision remain with the program.

faqs: Can heat included in rent qualify?
Yes, subject to the program’s assessment.
Is this enough to pay all winter costs?
DCF sends an annual review form.
Active Seasonal Fuel households qualify for free weatherization services.
